items.parentTitle: Social Conventions, Turn-Taking, and Formality in Language
items.whatStudentsLearn: In Level 3 English, children learn that effective cooperation depends on shared social conventions, adapting their spoken and written language between informal and formal situations.
items.whatThisMeans: Understanding how language changes depending on who you are speaking to (e.g. greeting a friend in the playground vs speaking politely to a school principal or shopkeeper).
items.whyItMatters: Builds clear interpersonal communication skills and social-emotional awareness.

homeActivities.title: Formal vs Casual Roleplay
homeActivities.description: Roleplay ordering at a restaurant or answering an official telephone call, comparing casual slang with polite formal phrasing.

items.parentTitle: Language of Emotion, Intensity, and Evaluation
items.whatStudentsLearn: Students explore how words can be adjusted to express stronger or milder emotions and evaluations (e.g. from 'okay' to 'good' to 'spectacular').
items.whatThisMeans: Choosing precise vocabulary to show exactly how someone feels instead of repeating simple words like 'nice' or 'bad'.
items.whyItMatters: Elevates student creative writing and descriptive detail, a core criterion in NAPLAN narrative and persuasive writing.

homeActivities.title: Emotion Thermometer
homeActivities.description: Pick a basic word like 'angry' or 'happy'. Have your child list words on a scale from warm to boiling hot (e.g. annoyed $\rightarrow$ frustrated $\rightarrow$ furious).

items.parentTitle: Discussing Characters and Settings in Diverse Literature
items.whatStudentsLearn: Children discuss how characters, settings, and events are represented in stories by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander authors and a wide range of Australian and international authors.
items.whatThisMeans: Exploring how a story's location, background, and culture shape what characters experience and how they solve problems.
items.whyItMatters: Develops cultural understanding, empathy, and literary appreciation.

homeActivities.title: Setting Explorer
homeActivities.description: While reading a bedtime book, discuss how the setting (e.g. the outback, an ocean reef, or a bustling city) influences what the characters can and cannot do.

items.parentTitle: Connecting Personal Experiences to Story Characters
items.whatStudentsLearn: Students discuss connections between their own lives and the experiences of characters in literary texts, giving reasons for their personal preferences.
items.whatThisMeans: Thinking about a time they felt like a character in a book, and explaining why they enjoyed or disliked a story using reasons.
items.whyItMatters: Deepens reading engagement, personal reflection, and critical thinking.

homeActivities.title: Book Review Chat
homeActivities.description: After finishing a chapter, ask your child: 'Did anything in this chapter remind you of something that happened in your own life?'

items.parentTitle: Using Interaction and Discussion Skills in Conversations
items.whatStudentsLearn: Children use conversational interaction skills (active listening, asking clarifying questions, building on ideas) to share information and perspectives.
items.whatThisMeans: Practicing how to listen attentively, wait for a natural pause to speak, and respond thoughtfully to what someone else said.
items.whyItMatters: Fundamental foundation for classroom discussions, oral presentations, and teamwork.

homeActivities.title: Dinner Table Topic Pass
homeActivities.description: Pick an interesting dinner question (e.g. 'If animals could talk, which one would be the funniest?'). Each person must acknowledge the previous speaker's idea before adding their own.
